description: Per-version migration guides (README documents the current library state; this file is the versioned upgrade history). Newest first. Downstreams read only the entries between their current and target versions.

field_notes.body_markdown: full guide in GitHub-flavored markdown (tables/code/steps preserved)

migrations.title: isPresentId, Eager field errors, upload progress without XHR
migrations.summary: isPresentId tests an Int64 id for presence; FieldError uses ChangeDetectionStrategy.Eager in place of the deprecated Default; the document upload bar is indeterminate until a progress event arrives; keel v1.3.1 changes no API sail uses.
migrations.body_markdown:
### Additive

- `isPresentId(value)`: true for an `Int64` above zero. keel sends an unset id as `'0'` or omits it, and `'0'` is truthy, so use it in place of `if (id)`.

### Behavioral

- `FieldError` declares `ChangeDetectionStrategy.Eager` (Angular 22's name for `Default`); its rendering is unchanged.
- `<sail-document-upload>` shows an indeterminate bar until an upload progress event arrives. Angular's default fetch backend sends none; add `withXhr()` to `provideHttpClient` for percent progress.
- `PartnerDocumentService.upload` omits `user_id` when `userId` is `'0'`.

migrations.title: Angular 22.2 peer dependencies
migrations.summary: The Angular peer dependencies require ^22.2.0, the version sail is built and checked with; v1.2.0 still declared ^21.0.0.
migrations.body_markdown:
### Breaking

- `@angular/core`, `common`, `forms`, `router`, `platform-browser`, `cdk` and `material` peers are `^22.2.0`. v1.2.0 declared `^21.0.0` although it requires Angular 22; skip v1.2.0 and move to v1.2.1 together with Angular 22.2.

migrations.title: Angular 22, 64-bit integers as strings, special characters, unique-key relations, agency authority, Scout v1.3.0
migrations.summary: Moves to Angular 22 and TypeScript 6.0, and adopts keel v1.2.135 to v1.2.138 and Scout v1.3.0: ids, minor-unit amounts and unbounded counts are Int64 strings across sail and sail/agent, the password validator enforces minSpecial, foreign keys pair with the parent columns they reference, invite acceptance follows AGENCY_DELEGATION/SET_ROLE, revokeDelegation takes the client, and checkout carries a currency and payment method types.
migrations.body_markdown:
Requires keel v1.2.138 (v1.3.0 changes no API sail uses) and, for `@nauticana/sail/agent`, Scout v1.2.20.

### Breaking

- Peer dependencies are Angular `^22.0.0` (core, common, forms, router, platform-browser, cdk, material), built with TypeScript `~6.0.3`; Angular 22's compiler needs Node `^22.22.3`, `^24.15.0` or `>=26`. Angular 21 is no longer supported.
- `Int64` (a decimal `string`), `isInt64`, `compareInt64` and `toSafeInteger` are exported from `util/integer`. Every id and foreign key is an `Int64`: `PartnerDocument`, `ApiKey`, `PartnerCredential`, `UserPaymentMethod`, `UserAccount.Id`, `TrustedDevice`, `ActiveSession`, `InboxMessage`, the agency models, and the `userId` / `partnerId` of login, OTP, social and token responses. Service methods take `Int64` ids (`revokeSession`, `revokeTrustedDevice`, `revokeApiKey`, `restrictApiKey`, `remove`, `setDefault`, `review`, `previewUrl`, `list`, `invite`, `cancel`, `setBillingModel`, `setPayoutProfile`); component inputs such as `userId` and `sail-oauth-connection-panel` `entityId` (default `'0'`, also on `OAuthConnectionService`) take an `Int64`.
- Minor-unit amounts (`PlanPrice.amountMinor`, `Subscription.installmentMinor`, `Invoice.totalMinor`, the agency `…Minor` fields) and unbounded counts (`UsageMeter.used` / `limit`, `PlanOverage.count` / `limit`, `PaginatedList.offset` / `total`, `InboxPage.unreadCount`, `AgencyService.clients().activeClients`) are `Int64`. Convert with `toSafeInteger` before arithmetic.
- `formatMinor`, `minorToDecimal`, `MoneyPipe`, `CurrencyService.format` / `formatLazy` and `MoneyColumnService.display` accept an `Int64` or a number. `formatMinor`, `minorToDecimal` and `parseMinor` (which returns an `Int64`) are exact across the 64-bit range.
- `DataType.BIGINT` (`'bigint'`) marks an `int8` column: generic forms keep its value as the typed digits and post them unchanged, its literal default stays a string, and a table action parameter with `dataType` `bigint` is a text input checked as an integer and posted as a string. A money column (`CurrencyPath`) renders whether its value arrives as a number or an `Int64`.
- Bounded values stay numbers: exponents, `termCount`, `trialDays`, `seats`, `resendCountdownSec`, `defaultCommissionRateBp`, `payingClients`, `PaginatedList.limit`, `PartnerDocument.VersionNo` and the `TableColumn` metadata.
- `PasswordRules.minSpecial` is required; the validator and `passwordPolicyHint` enforce it, count the length in characters rather than UTF-16 units, and name counts above one ("2 numbers").
- `ForeignKey.ParentColumns` names the parent columns `Columns` reference. Foreign-key seeding in forms and lookups, and currency-path parent lookups, pair with it instead of the parent's primary key, so a key such as `(partner_id, provider_id)` → `(partner_id, id)` fills both columns. A foreign key whose lists differ in length is logged and skipped.
- `AgencyService.revokeDelegation(clientPartnerId)` requires the client's `Int64` id: only the delegated agency revokes, with `AGENCY` / `MANAGE_CLIENTS`. A client removes its agency's access with `setDelegationRoles([])`. `setDelegationRoles(roles, clientPartnerId?)` omits the client to act for the session partner instead of sending `0`.
- `@nauticana/sail/agent` follows Scout v1.2.20, which writes every Go `int` and `int64` as a string. These are `Int64`: Studio revisions (`agent_revision`, `type_defaults_revision`, every `expected_…_revision`), versions (`published_version`, `active_version`, `AgentRelease.version`, `ReleaseActivation.version`, `StudioFeature.version`, `template_version`), ids (`prompt_header_id`, `published_by`, `bound_by`, `user_id`, `ReleaseActivation.id`, `SafetyEvent.id`, `DecisionRecord.id`, `execution_step_id`, `revises_step_id`, `Confirmation.tenant_id` / `id`), `route_step`, `AgentReleaseSection.sequence`, `latency_ms`, `input_tokens`, `output_tokens`, `credits`, `canary_percentage`, `attempts`, `duration_ms`, `ConversationTurn.cost_minor` / `exponent`, `DecisionPage.next_before`, and on turn events `v`, `progress.iteration`, `extension.v` and `citations[].position`. The model credit rates and `ConversationStreamError.status` stay numbers. Send revisions back as received.
- `TurnReplyFrame.sequence` and `TurnStream.cursor()` are `Int64`; `TurnStream` compares and steps them exactly, and `accept` refuses a frame whose sequence is not an `Int64`. An app transport passes Scout's frames through unchanged.
- `AgentStudioService.releaseSections(name, version)`, `decisions(before)` and `safetyEvents(name, before)` take `Int64` values; an empty `before` reads the first page. `PromptResetTarget.prompt_header_id` is `'0'` for every section.

### Behavioral

- `AgencyAcceptComponent` waits for the user's permissions and offers the accept button only with `AGENCY_DELEGATION` / `SET_ROLE` on `agency_client_delegation` (keel v1.2.138, seeded for `PARTNER_ADMIN`). Without it, or after a 403, it says an administrator of the client must accept and offers business setup, since keel refuses a user without a business with the same 403.

### Additive

- `CheckoutRequest.currency` (ISO 4217) and `paymentMethodTypes`, and the matching `sail-checkout-button` inputs `[currency]` and `[paymentMethodTypes]`; a setup session with neither offers cards.
- `ApprovalRequest.authenticated_only`: the approval inbox labels such a request as having no decision links and decides it as any other.

migrations.title: reCAPTCHA v3 and Turnstile rendering
migrations.summary: Adds the recaptcha_v3 provider (keel v1.2.133) to <sail-human-challenge> and fixes Turnstile, which never rendered.
migrations.body_markdown:
### Behavioral

- `turnstile` renders: the component no longer calls `turnstile.ready()`, which Turnstile refuses after an async script load, so v1.1.49 always emitted `(failed)`.

### Additive

- `HumanVerifierProvider` gains `recaptcha_v3`; `SailGuiConfig.humanVerifier.action` (default `signup`) names the action keel's `human_verifier_action` expects.
- `HumanChallengeComponent.fetchToken(): Promise<string>` resolves the token to send (the widget's current token, or a fresh v3 token) and retries a failed load and rejects when the provider still cannot load; `awaitsToken()` is true while a widget still has to be passed and false after a failed load. `RegisterComponent` fetches the token at submit; an OTP register form should do the same instead of reading only the `(token)` output.

migrations.title: Human verification and pending OTP signups
migrations.summary: Adopts keel v1.2.132: a challenge widget for registration, challengeToken on register sends, isNewUser on OTP verify, and resendOtp without a purpose.
migrations.body_markdown:
### Breaking

- `resendOtp(otpToken, purpose?)` → `resendOtp(otpToken)`; `OtpResendRequest` has no `purpose`. keel resends with the purpose bound at send.
- `OtpVerifyResponse.isNewUser: boolean` is required. A register send for an unknown contact no longer creates the account; it exists after a successful verify, so anything that read user data after `sendOtp` moves to after `verifyOtp` and branches on `isNewUser`.

### Additive

- `SailGuiConfig.humanVerifier: { provider: 'turnstile' | 'hcaptcha' | 'recaptcha', siteKey }` from the host app's environment (keel does not serve the site key).
- `<sail-human-challenge (token)>` (`HumanChallengeComponent`) renders the configured widget and emits the token, `''` on expiry and `(failed)` when the script cannot load; `reset()` after a refused submit. Renders nothing without a site key.
- `OtpRequest.challengeToken` and `PartnerRegistration.challengeToken`, passed through by `sendOtp` and `register`. `RegisterComponent` mounts the widget and sends the token.

migrations.title: Money columns from metadata, partner document type filter
migrations.summary: Metadata-driven tables, forms, lookups and reports show and edit money columns keel marks with TableColumn.CurrencyPath at the catalog exponent; the partner documents list filters by type. Adopts keel v1.2.131.
migrations.body_markdown:
### Additive

- `TableColumn.CurrencyPath` (keel v1.2.131 `column_display_attribute.currency_path`): `TableList`, `TableDetail`, `TableLookup`, `TableReport` and the read-only form render the column through `MoneyColumnService` at the row's currency exponent; the edit field takes a decimal with the currency code as suffix and stores minor units. Ancestor rows a dotted path needs are taken from the parent a child grid is nested under or fetched once through generic REST, so the role needs `TABLE SELECT` on those tables and on `currency`.
- `BaseTable.displayValue(field, value, record?)`: pass the row to format a money column. `BaseTable.parentRow()` names the row a view is nested under; `TableDetail`, `TableForm` and `DynamicField` override it.
- `<sail-dynamic-field [record] [parent]>` and `<sail-record-form [parent]>` carry the row and its parent to the money editor.
- `CurrencyService.exponentLazy(currency)` and `formatLazy(minor, currency)` start the catalog load and answer `undefined` / `''` until it is ready (`sailMoney` now uses them). `minorToDecimal(minor, exponent)` is `parseMinor`'s inverse.
- `BaseAuthService.apiNameFor(tableName)` finds the generic REST api serving a table.
- `<sail-partner-documents [documentTypes]>` limits the list to the given `document_type` codes, like the review queue.

migrations.title: Money input parsing, document review filters, configurable deletion cancel
migrations.summary: Adds parseMinor for typed amounts, member and type filters plus a reviewed output on the document review queue, a read-only mode for partner documents, and a configurable Cancel link on account deletion. No keel change.
migrations.body_markdown:
### Additive

- `parseMinor(text, exponent)` turns a typed decimal into minor units exactly; `null` for malformed text, unsafe integers or more fraction digits than the exponent.
- `<sail-document-review-queue>`: `[userId]`, `[documentTypes]` and `(reviewed)` emitting `{ id, approved }`. `PartnerDocumentService.pending(userId?)` and `list(userId?, status?)`.
- `<sail-partner-documents [allowReupload]="false">` hides "Upload replacement".
- `<sail-account-deletion [cancelRoute]>` sets the Cancel link (default `/dashboard`); `null` hides it.

migrations.title: Server-side list sort, unsaved-change guard, shared confirmations, plan-change offers
migrations.summary: Generic lists keep sort and page in the URL and sort on the server; edit dialogs guard unsaved changes; native alert() and confirm() are replaced by Material dialogs; invalid forms stay submittable and point to the error. Adopts keel v1.2.126: a plan change can name the offer it moves to.
migrations.body_markdown:
Requires keel v1.2.126 for `changePlan` offers; everything else needs no keel change.

### Behavioral

- `TableList` treats `_order`, `_limit` and `_offset` as list controls, reads and writes them in the URL, and sends `orderBy` to keel. Client-side per-page sorting and `sortedRecords` are removed; bind `records()`.
- `TableList` shows a progress bar and `aria-busy` while loading, and distinguishes an empty table (`[emptyMessage]`, default "No {caption} yet") from a search with no matches (filters plus Clear search). The "No records found." text is gone.
- Native `alert()` and `confirm()` are replaced: `PromptService` confirms deletes, revocations, discards, `TableAction.confirmMessage` and the route guard; saving a record is no longer confirmed. `BaseAuthService.canDeactivate` may return `Observable<boolean>`. `BaseTable.requireAuth` and action failures go through `reportError()`, which table views show in their alert region.
- `TableEdit` reports `hasUnsavedChanges()` and confirms Cancel and close when dirty; `TableList` keeps its dialog open across navigation (`closeOnNavigation: false`) and answers the guard for it.
- Submit buttons no longer disable for an invalid form; the handler marks controls touched and focuses the first invalid field.
- `DynamicField` uses `readonly` instead of `disabled` for read-only inputs and textareas, and shows a read-only boolean as "Yes" or "No".
- `sail-navigation` adds a skip link and a focusable `<main id="sail-main">`; generated routes get titles. Style `.sail-skip-link` and `.sail-main`.
- `ConnectionPanel` reports a passing test in `.connection-panel__notice` and shows `LastChecked` on the tile.

### Additive

- `PromptService`, `ConfirmDialog`/`ConfirmOptions`, `FieldError` (`<mat-error sailFieldError>`), `submittable()`, `BaseForm.hasUnsavedChanges()`, `TableList` `emptyMessage` input.
- `BillingService.changePlan(planId, offer?: PlanOffer)` sends the offer's `billingCycle`, `termType` and `termCount` (a `PlanPrice` fits), so a subscriber can switch billing cycle on the same plan or move to another plan on another cycle; omitted keeps the current terms. Replace an app-local support hand-off for cycle changes with it.

migrations.title: Deep links survive a full page load
migrations.summary: BaseAuthService lands the first route build on the address the page loaded with.
migrations.body_markdown:
No keel change.

### Behavioral

- `BaseAuthService` records the page's path and query when it is constructed with a stored session, before Angular's first navigation, and the first route build lands there unless it is the root or a `/login` route. A menu route loaded directly, such as an OAuth connect return with its ticket, no longer falls to the pre-login catch-all and then the dashboard. `setLanding()` still wins. Remove an app initializer that called `setLanding()` with the page's own address.

migrations.title: Plan-change overages
migrations.summary: Adopts keel v1.2.125: BillingService checks a plan change for resources the target plan does not allow.
migrations.body_markdown:
Requires keel v1.2.125.

### Additive

- `BillingService.checkChange(planId)` reads `POST /api/billing/subscription/change/check` and returns `{ overages: PlanOverage[] }` (`resource`, `caption`, `count`, `limit`), empty when the change is allowed. `changePlan` refuses an exceeded paid target with 409 carrying the same overages. Replace an app-local client and model of this endpoint with these.

migrations.title: Browser time zone on keel requests
migrations.summary: Adopts keel v1.2.118: keel requests carry the browser time zone, and timestamps arrive as RFC 3339.
migrations.body_markdown:
Requires keel v1.2.118.

### Behavioral

- `authInterceptor` sends `X-Time-Zone` (the browser's IANA zone, read once per page load) on every keel `/api/` and `/public/` request, signed in or not; keel renders emails, notifications and exports in it. Other origins receive no sail headers.
- keel v1.2.118 sends billing and device timestamps as RFC 3339 UTC; `<sail-scheduled-change-banner>` passes `scheduledAt` straight to the `date` pipe. Remove any app-side parser for the old `2026-11-12 00:00:00 +0000 UTC` layout.

migrations.title: Scheduled plan changes
migrations.summary: Adopts keel v1.2.117: a subscription reports a scheduled change, changePlan returns its outcome, and a banner offers to keep the current plan.
migrations.body_markdown:
Requires keel v1.2.117.

### Breaking

- `BillingService.changePlan(planId)` returns `Observable<PlanChangeResult>` (`{ status: 'changed' | 'scheduled' }`) instead of `Observable<void>`. Re-selecting the current plan resumes renewal and clears a scheduled change.

### Additive

- `Subscription.scheduledPlanId?` and `scheduledAt?`: the plan that starts when the current one ends, and when.
- `<sail-scheduled-change-banner [subscription] [plans] (kept)>` names the ending plan, its end date and the plan that follows, with a Keep my plan action. Replace an app-local notice with it.

migrations.title: Disconnect through the connect route
migrations.summary: OAuthConnectionService.disconnect posts to keel's connect disconnect route instead of deleting the partner_credential row.
migrations.body_markdown:
Requires keel v1.2.115 (unchanged from v1.1.39).

### Breaking

- `OAuthConnectionService.disconnect(id)` becomes `disconnect(provider, entityId = 0)` and posts `POST /api/oauth/disconnect`, so keel's `DisconnectConnection` runs and announces the change. `<sail-oauth-connection-panel>` uses it; the role no longer needs a generic `DELETE` grant on `partner_credential` for it.

migrations.title: Billing captions, provider-managed subscriptions, OAuth-only connection test
migrations.summary: Adopts keel v1.2.115: usage meters show the resource caption, provider actions hide for a subscription the provider does not manage, and the status chip reads the seeded subscription_status domain.
migrations.body_markdown:
Requires keel v1.2.115.

### Breaking

- `UsageMeter.caption` and `Subscription.providerManaged` are required; build fixtures with them.

### Behavioral

- `<sail-status-chip>` defaults `domain` to `subscription_status` (was `SUBSCRIPTION_STATUS`, which matched no seeded domain and rendered the code).
- `<sail-usage-meter>` labels a meter by `caption`, falling back to `resource`.
- `<sail-portal-button>` and `<sail-dunning-banner>` take `[providerManaged]` (default `true`); pass `Subscription.providerManaged` to hide the portal button for a subscription the provider does not hold. Gate app cancel and plan-change actions the same way.
- `<sail-oauth-connection-panel>` shows **Test** only for `authType: 'oauth'`; keel serves no test route for an API-key connection.

migrations.title: Addressable conversation agents
migrations.summary: ConversationService lists the agents of a type the signed-in person may address.
migrations.body_markdown:
Requires the agent entry point's Scout v1.2.16 conversation bridge (unchanged from v1.1.37).

### Additive

- `ConversationService.agents(agentType)` reads `GET {base}agents?agent_type=` and returns `ConversationAgent[]` (`agent_name`, `display_name`, `is_default`, `release`), default first. Pass a chosen `agent_name` on `ConversationTurnRequest` to address that agent instead of the type's default. Replace an app-local client and model of this endpoint with these.

migrations.title: Approval inbox summary, withdraw step and history window; API key scope domains
migrations.summary: Adopts keel v1.2.114 and Scout v1.2.16: the approval inbox names confirmations through a summary function, confirms withdrawal inline and bounds its history; API keys load scopes from constant domains.
migrations.body_markdown:
Requires keel v1.2.114; the agent entry point requires Scout v1.2.16.

### Breaking

- `ApprovalInboxComponent.confirming` holds the pending step (`''`, `'approve'`, `'withdraw'`); `askApprove()` and `cancelApprove()` become `ask(step)` and `cancelAsk()`.

### Additive

- `<sail-approval-inbox>`: `[summary]` (`(c: Confirmation) => string`, default the tool code) names a confirmation in the list and heading; `[historyDays]` (default 30) and `[limit]` (default 200) bound the confirmations listed.
- `ApprovalService.confirmations(since, limit)`.
- `<sail-api-keys [scopeDomains]>`: constant ids whose values are offered after `[scopes]`.
- `GuardrailRule.reason`.

### Behavioral

- Withdrawing a confirmation asks inline instead of through `window.confirm`.
- The inbox requests closed confirmations created within `historyDays`, at most `limit`, instead of Scout's whole default batch.

Replace `[scopes]` built from `LabelService` with `[scopeDomains]`, and pass `[summary]` where a tool code is not readable.

migrations.title: Approval inbox parity, labels, API key expiry and turn thread fallbacks
migrations.summary: Adopts keel v1.2.113 and Scout v1.2.14: the approval inbox groups, previews, labels and confirms; activity shows labels; API keys take an expiry; the turn thread has fallbacks and a typed template context.
migrations.body_markdown:
Requires keel v1.2.113; the agent entry point requires Scout v1.2.14.

### Breaking

- `<sail-assistant-activity [who]>` is removed; set Scout's `Labeler` on `StudioDecisionsHandler.Labels` to name principals and apps.
- `AccessService.mintApiKey(keyName, scopes, allowedCidrs)` becomes `mintApiKey(NewApiKey)` (keel's `generate` request, with `expires_at`).
- `ApprovalService.reconcileConfirmation` requires its note and takes a `ReconcileOutcome`.
- `AgentSummary.readiness` and `AGENT_READINESS_CAPTIONS` are typed by the new `AgentReadiness` union.

### Additive

- `PrincipalRef.label`, `DecisionRecord.client_label`, `Confirmation.tenant_label` and `client_label`, and `principalName(ref)`.
- `<sail-approval-inbox>`: `[open]` (an item key or a linked confirmation id), sections (`groupInbox`), `<ng-template sailApprovalPreview="tool" let-c>` (`"*"` for any tool), `CONFIRMATION_NOTE_MAX`.
- `<sail-turn-thread>`: `[failedText]`, `sailTurnResult="*"`, and `TurnResultContext` typing `let-turn`.
- `<sail-api-keys>`: an expiry field and column; `[scopes]` is optional, and without a selection keel's `ScopePolicy` supplies the scopes.
- `httpStatus(err)`.

### Behavioral

- The inbox loads approvals and confirmations independently; a list answering `404` stays empty. Approving or confirming asks once more, reconciling requires a note, 403 and 404 have their own messages, a 404 reloads the list, and focus moves to the decision after an action.

Upgrade the backend libraries, set the Scout `Labeler` on the approval and Studio decisions handlers, and replace `[who]` and `mintApiKey` call sites.

migrations.title: Minor-unit money, API keys, connected apps, assistant activity, turn thread and Studio guardrails
migrations.summary: Adopts keel v1.2.112 and Scout v1.2.13: minor-unit money, catalog-backed country and currency data, API keys and connected apps, assistant activity, turn threads, the confirmation inbox and Studio guardrails.
migrations.body_markdown:
Requires keel v1.2.112; the agent entry point requires Scout v1.2.13.

### Breaking

- Replace `formatCurrency` and `formatMinorCurrency` with `formatMinor(minor, currency, exponent)` or `sailMoney`. Billing models now use their minor-unit fields and exponents; `PublicPlan.priceId` is removed and its current keel fields are required.
- `CountryProfile`, `DEFAULT_COUNTRY_PROFILES` and the bank form's `countryProfiles` input are removed. The form reads keel's `country` table and `tax_id_type` domain.

### Additive

- `ApiKeysComponent`, `ConnectedAppsComponent`, `AccessService` and their models. API-key action URLs and grants come from backend metadata; `RestURL.oauthGrantsURL` and `oauthGrantRevokeURL` default to keel's `GrantHandler` routes.
- `@nauticana/sail/agent`: `AssistantActivityComponent` over `AgentStudioService.decisions` (Scout's `decisions` feature), `TurnThreadComponent` over `ConversationService.turns` (`ConversationTurn`, `ConversationTurnPage`, `TurnStatus`, `TERMINAL_TURN_STATUSES`), `<sail-approval-inbox>` confirmation rows over `ApprovalService.confirmations`, `decideConfirmation`, `withdrawConfirmation`, `reconcileConfirmation` (`Confirmation`, `ConfirmationKey`, `ConfirmationStatus`), a Studio Guardrails tab, and `AGENT_READINESS_CAPTIONS`.
- `DecisionRecord` is Scout's wire type: `id` is a number, `evidence_digest` replaces `evidence`, and `client_ref` and `work_ref` are added.
- `CurrencyService`, `MoneyPipe`, `Currency` and `Country`. Amounts lacking an exponent require `TABLE SELECT currency`; the bank form requires `TABLE SELECT country`.

### Behavioral

- `sailCaption` no longer writes a signal during a cached domain's render.

Upgrade the backend libraries, replace removed money fields and formatters, grant the catalog and API-key operations each screen uses, and remove `countryProfiles` bindings.

migrations.title: Apple first-authorization name, code re-authentication, Studio page and approval inbox on Scout v1.2.8
migrations.summary: SocialLoginComponent passes Apple's first-authorization name to the app, and accounts without a password re-authenticate with a one-time code. @nauticana/sail/agent moves to Scout v1.2.8 and adds an embeddable Studio page and an approval inbox.
migrations.body_markdown:
Requires keel v1.2.102 for `POST /api/user/reauth/send` (`OTPHandler.GetAuthRoutes`). Apps that do not import `@nauticana/sail/agent` take only the additive core changes and need no Scout; the agent entry point requires Scout v1.2.8.

### Additive (`@nauticana/sail`)

- `LoginResponseSocial.socialName?: SocialName` carries the name Apple returns only on first authorization; pre-fill the profile from it.
- `ReauthCredentials.reauthCode`, `BaseAuthService.sendReauthCode(channel?)`, `RestURL.reauthSendURL`, `ReauthChannel`, and `ReauthSendResponse`. `<sail-account-deletion reauthMethod="code">` starts on the code path; the user can switch.
- `CaptionPipe` (`sailCaption`) renders a code's backend caption; `LabelService.loadLabels` also serves catalog tables registered in `foreign_key_lookup`, by table name.

### Breaking (`@nauticana/sail/agent`)

- `ConversationTurnRequest.agent_id` → `agent_type`, plus optional `agent_name`, `release`, `release_reason`, `work_ref`.
- `AgentMergeMode` is `'R' | 'A' | 'I'` (was `'replace' | 'append'`); `DecisionOutcome` is `'A' | 'D' | 'P'` (was `'allow' | 'deny' | 'pending'`).
- `AgentDraft.approval_policy`, `AgentApprovalPolicy`, and `AgentRelease.require_approval` are removed; approval is an `approval_routing` or policy setting.
- `AgentAuditEvent.user_id` is optional, set only when a person acted.

### Additive (`@nauticana/sail/agent`)

- `AgentStudioService.features`, `create`, `rename`, `archive`, `unarchive`, `settings`, `saveSetting` with their types; `AgentSummary.archived`, `AgentPromptLayer.bound_by`, publish `canary_percentage` and `effective_at`, `AgentRelease.activation`.
- `<sail-studio-page>` with `sailStudioTab` product tabs, `diffReleaseSections`, and `studioErrorMessage`.
- `ApprovalService` and `<sail-approval-inbox>` over Scout's approval desk.
- The `citations` turn event renders as a link list. An empty turn-level `approval_pending` no longer adds a blank tool row.

### Migration

Core only: no change required. Agent entry point: upgrade Scout to v1.2.8, send `agent_type` on turn submit, map decision outcomes and merge modes to their codes, and drop `approval_policy` from draft handling.

migrations.title: Sign-in prompt, new-device step-up and sessions
migrations.summary: Adopts keel v1.2.106. The login page honors prompt=login and prompt=select_account instead of handing off the stored session, the 2FA step accepts an emailed new-device code, every session-minting call sends the keel_device cookie, and SessionsComponent lists and signs out sign-in sessions.
migrations.body_markdown:
Requires keel v1.2.106.

### Behavioral

- Login pages with a valid `return` honor `prompt=login` and `prompt=select_account`: the stored session is not adopted (`isLoggedIn` stays false) until `continueSession()`, and a fresh sign-in, including its 2FA step, keeps the query.
- Any sign-in revokes the refresh token it replaces.
- `loginSocial`, `verifyOtp`, and `confirmRegister` send credentials so `keel_device` round-trips.
- `errorDetail` provides messages for `signin_network`, `signin_network_lockout`, and `stepup_unavailable`.

### Additive

- `LoginResponse2FA.twoFactorMethod?: 'email'` identifies emailed new-device codes.
- `BaseAuthService.signInPrompt`, `continueSession()`, and `signOutHere()` support OAuth account selection.
- `ActiveSession`, the session URLs and auth methods, and `SessionsComponent` expose session listing and revocation.

### Migration

Upgrade keel to v1.2.106, keep credentialed CORS for the SPA origin, and optionally route `SessionsComponent`.

migrations.title: OAuth connect flow completes a callback ticket
migrations.summary: Adopts keel v1.2.101. The provider callback no longer creates the connection or redirects with ?<provider>=success. keel parks the validated callback under a single-use ticket and redirects to FrontendReturnURL?connect=<provider>&ticket=<ticket>; the connection panel redeems it as the signed-in user through the new /api/oauth/<provider>/complete route.
migrations.body_markdown:
Requires keel v1.2.101. keel binds a provider connection to the user who started it (RFC 6749 §10.12).

### Breaking

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Return URL after provider consent | `FrontendReturnURL?<provider>=success`; the callback had already stored the connection | `FrontendReturnURL?connect=<provider>&ticket=<ticket>`; nothing is stored until the ticket is redeemed |
| `OAuthConnectionPanelComponent.ngOnInit` | recorded `?<provider>=success`, stripped it, confirmed the row on reload | strips `connect` and `ticket` (hash preserved), ignores an unconfigured provider, posts the ticket with the user's bearer token, then confirms the row on reload and emits `connected` as before |
| Page hosting the panel at `FrontendReturnURL` | could be public | must require sign-in before the panel runs; the completion call needs the bearer token of the user who started the flow |

### Additive

| | |
|---|---|
| `OAuthConnectionService.completeOAuth(provider, ticket)` | `POST /api/oauth/<provider>/complete` with `{ticket}` → `{status, provider}` |
| Panel messages | 403 (started by another user or partner) and 400 (missing, expired per `oauth_state_ttl_seconds`, spent, or another provider's ticket) each show a distinct "start again" message; other failures show keel's detail or a generic message |

Unchanged: provider redirect URIs, `startOAuth`, `testConnection`, `saveApiKey`, `list`, `disconnect`.

### Migration steps

1. Upgrade keel to v1.2.101 and keep `FrontendReturnURL` pointing at the page that hosts `<sail-oauth-connection-panel>`.
2. Guard that route with the app's authenticated guard if it was public.
3. Remove any app code that looked for `?<provider>=success`.

migrations.title: Tenant single sign-on and DNS or HTTP-file domain verification
migrations.summary: Adopts keel v1.2.100. Opt-in organization sign-in and its return page, a protocol-aware identity provider configure dialog, masked secret action parameters, and DNS TXT or HTTP-file domain verification through the DOMAIN_VERIFIER port.
migrations.body_markdown:
Requires keel v1.2.100 for single sign-on and for DNS or HTTP-file domain verification. Nothing changes until an app opts in.

### Additive

| | |
|---|---|
| `SailGuiConfig.ssoLogin` | shows `<sail-sso-login>` on `<sail-login>` |
| `SsoLoginComponent` (`sail-sso-login`) | navigates to `RestURL.ssoStartURL` with the email |
| `SsoReturnComponent` (`sail-sso-return`) | keel's return URL: exchanges `code` once, shows `error` and test outcomes |
| `SSO_ERROR_MESSAGES`, `ssoErrorMessage()`, `SailGuiConfig.ssoErrorMessages` | wording of keel's single sign-on error codes |
| `RestURL.ssoStartURL`, `RestURL.ssoSamlMetadataURL` | `/public/sso/start`, `/public/sso/saml/metadata` |
| `BaseAuthService.setLanding(url)` | the next route build lands on `url` instead of the dashboard |
| `BaseAuthService.hasPermission(object, action, value)` | checks any grant against its low-limit value |
| action parameter `dataType` `secret` / `password` | masked input, posted as a string |
| `partner_identity_provider` `configure` | filters protocol and client-auth fields and masks the client secret |
| `DomainVerifier.challenge?(domain, method)`, `confirm(domain, code, method?)` | DNS TXT (`DT`) and HTTP file (`HF`) challenges |
| `<sail-domain-verification [methods]>` | methods offered, default `['EC']` |

## Adopting it

1. For single sign-on, set `ssoLogin: true`, route `login/sso` to `SsoReturnComponent`, and set keel's `SSOHandler.FrontendReturnURL` to that route.
2. For DNS or HTTP-file domain verification, implement `challenge` on the `DOMAIN_VERIFIER` provider (post keel's `partner_domain` `challenge` action and emit its `challenge`), pass `method` through `confirm`, and pass `[methods]`.

migrations.title: Password change on keel's routes
migrations.summary: Adopts keel v1.2.99. Password change, forgot-password and reset post keel's /public/password/change, /forgot and /reset. A successful change or reset ends the session immediately, because keel revokes every refresh token, and the login page asks the user to sign in again.
migrations.body_markdown:
Requires keel v1.2.99.

### Breaking

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `RestURL.chpassURL` | `/public/login/chpass` (not a keel route) | `/public/password/change` |
| `RestURL.confirmChpassURL` | `/public/confirm/password` (not a keel route) | `/public/password/reset` |
| `forgotPassword()` | posted `chpassURL` | posts the new `RestURL.forgotPasswordURL` (`/public/password/forgot`) |
| `chpass()`, `forgotPassword()`, `confirmChpass()` response type | `{message}` | `{status}`, as keel answers |

### Behavioral

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| successful `chpass()` / `confirmChpass()` | a signed-in session was kept until the next refresh failed, then ended as `login?sessionExpired=true` | clears the session and routes to `login?passwordChanged=true` |
| `ChpassComponent` on success | showed a success message | leaves for the login page |
| `<sail-login>` | — | shows a sign-in-again notice for `?passwordChanged=true` |

## Adopting it

1. Delete `configureRestUrls` overrides that pointed `chpassURL`, `forgotPasswordURL` or `confirmChpassURL` at keel's `/public/password/*` routes.
2. Remove app code that logged the user out or refreshed the session after a password change.
3. Read `status` instead of `message` from the password responses.
4. A custom login page should render a notice for `?passwordChanged=true`.

migrations.title: Signup on keel's registration routes
migrations.summary: Adopts keel v1.2.94. Confirmation posts to /public/register/confirm and signs the user in from the tokens it answers. PartnerRegistration is typed after keel's camelCase JSON. BaseAuthService gains createPartner() for the signed-in partner step and exchangeHandoff() for keel's single-use sign-in code.
migrations.body_markdown:
Requires keel v1.2.94; older keel answers 404 on the confirmation route.

### Breaking

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `RestURL.confirmRegisterURL` = `/public/confirm/register` | `/public/register/confirm` |
| `PartnerRegistration` with PascalCase fields (`FirstName`, `PartnerCaption`, `DomainURL`, `PlanID`, …) | `AccountRegistration & Partial<PartnerSetup>` with keel's camelCase fields (`firstName`, `partnerCaption`, `domainUrl`, `planId`, …); partner fields are optional |
| `PartnerRegistration.Latitude` / `Longitude`: `number \| null` | `latitude?` / `longitude?`: omit when unknown |
| `ConfirmRegisterResponse` = `{status, partnerId, planId, paymentRequired, paymentUrl?}` | extends `TokenPair`; `planId`, `paymentRequired`, `paymentUrl` are present only when the registration carried a partner |
| `register()` typed as answering a `PartnerRegistration` | answers `{status: string}` |

### Behavioral

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `confirmRegister()` | returned the response only | also completes the login (stores the token pair, loads appdata, initialises routes) |
| `ConfirmRegisterComponent` without a payment URL | navigated to `/login/local` | stays signed in; the post-login navigation applies |

### Additive

- `createPartner(setup: PartnerSetup): Observable<PartnerCreated>` posts `RestURL.registerPartnerURL` (`/api/register/partner`), rotates the refresh token, restarts the session on the new JWT and emits keel's result.
- `exchangeHandoff(code)` posts `RestURL.registerExchangeURL` (`/public/register/exchange`) and routes the answer like `login()`, including the 2FA step.
- Types `AccountRegistration`, `PartnerSetup<TExtra>`, `PartnerCreated`.

## Adopting it

1. Rename the fields of any hand-built `PartnerRegistration` to camelCase.
2. Remove a login or `acceptToken()` call that followed `confirmRegister()`, and do not navigate from its handler.
3. Replace app-local calls to the partner-setup and hand-off-exchange routes, and their request and response types, with `createPartner()` and `exchangeHandoff()`. Drop the `refreshSession()` and `acceptToken()` that followed partner setup.

migrations.title: OAuth hand-off for a signed-in user
migrations.summary: Adopts keel v1.2.93, whose login redirect sends `return` as the absolute authorize URL. A user who is already signed in and opens the login page with an allowed `?return=` is handed off without signing in again.
migrations.body_markdown:
### Behavioral

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `loadStoredSession()` on a `/login` route with an allowed `?return=` and `oauthServerUrl` set | loaded appdata and routed to the dashboard | posts the session hand-off and leaves for keel's `redirect`; appdata and routes are not loaded |
| hand-off answered 401 | `sessionHandoffError` set | rotates the refresh token once and retries; a second failure sets `sessionHandoffError` |

The hand-off still requires an absolute `return` whose host is in `allowedReturnHosts`.

## Adopting it

1. Upgrade the backend to keel v1.2.93 so its login redirect sends an absolute `return`; older keel sends a path, which sail ignores.
2. Point keel's `OAuthASHandler.LoginURL` at a route under `/login` that calls `loadStoredSession()` (sail's navigation shell does).

migrations.title: OAuth sign-in through keel's session hand-off; subscription grants; agency delegation roles
migrations.summary: Adopts keel v1.2.89. A login carrying ?return= is handed to the authorization server through keel's POST /oauth/session/handoff instead of an app session-cookie endpoint; SailGuiConfig.sessionCookieUrl is replaced by oauthServerUrl. Subscription cancel, plan change and the billing portal now need a grant, and a 403 is reported as not permitted. Agency delegations carry a role set with per-role expiry.
migrations.body_markdown:
### Breaking

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `SailGuiConfig.sessionCookieUrl` (app endpoint mirroring the JWT into a cookie) | `SailGuiConfig.oauthServerUrl` — base URL of keel's OAuth authorization server |
| login POSTs `sessionCookieUrl` with `withCredentials`, then navigates to `?return=` | login POSTs `{"return": <raw ?return=>}` with the bearer JWT to `{oauthServerUrl}/oauth/session/handoff`, then navigates to the `redirect` keel answers |
| `AgencyDelegation` without roles | `AgencyDelegation.roles: AgencyRoleGrant[]` is required |

`allowedReturnHosts` is unchanged and still gates the `?return=` value. The request does not opt into cross-origin cookies or send a CSRF token; keel sets the authorization server's HttpOnly cookie while redeeming the redirect. A relative `?return=` is no longer accepted.

### Additive

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| agency model | none | `AgencyRoleGrant { role, expiresAt? }`, `AgencyClient.roles?` |
| `AgencyService` | none | `setDelegationRoles(roles, clientPartnerId = 0)` — POST `RestURL.agencyDelegationRolesURL` (`/api/v1/agency/delegation/roles`); replaces the whole set, an empty list removes access without revoking |
| errors | none | `isPermissionDenied(err)` — true for HTTP 403 |

### Behavioral

- A failed hand-off sets `sessionHandoffError` and never redirects: 400 means keel rejected the return URL, 401 means sign in again to retry. A `redirect` outside `oauthServerUrl`'s origin is not followed.
- `<sail-portal-button>` reports a 403 as not permitted. keel v1.2.89 answers 403 on `/api/billing/subscription/cancel`, `/change` and `/api/billing/portal` without `PARTNER_PLAN_SUBSCRIPTION` `CANCEL` / `CHANGE` / `PORTAL` (seeded for `PARTNER_ADMIN`).

## Adopting it

1. Replace `sessionCookieUrl` with `oauthServerUrl` from app configuration and delete the app's session-cookie endpoint. Set `OAuthASHandler.Handoff` and `UserService` on the keel side, use `handler.HandoffSessionUser` as `ResolveUser`, and allow the SPA origin by CORS on the authorization server.
2. Grant `PARTNER_PLAN_SUBSCRIPTION` actions to any role besides `PARTNER_ADMIN` that changes subscriptions; callers of `cancelSubscription()` / `changePlan()` should branch on `isPermissionDenied(err)`.
3. Render delegation roles from the `agency_delegation_role` constant catalogue (`LabelService.options`); do not hardcode codes. `setDelegationRoles` answers 422 for an unknown, duplicate or blank role, more than 32 roles, or an expiry not in the future, and 403 without `AGENCY_DELEGATION` / `SET_ROLE`.

migrations.title: Saved cards are removed through keel's remove action; partner-document uploads; live inbox
migrations.summary: UserPaymentMethodService.delete becomes remove, posting to keel v1.2.79's detach-then-delete table action. Table-action parameters accept files and post multipart, and the partner-document service and components cover keel's document workflow. LabelService gains options() and requireLabel(). The notification inbox follows keel's realtime notification frames, which RealtimeService.userFrames() previously dropped.
migrations.body_markdown:
### Breaking

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `UserPaymentMethodService.delete(id)` (generic CRUD DELETE) | `remove(id)` — POST `{id}` to keel's `user_payment_method/remove` table action (`RestURL.paymentMethodRemoveURL`) |
| `<sail-user-payment-methods (deleted)>` | `(removed)` |

keel v1.2.79 detaches the card at the provider before deleting the row and withdraws the generic `TABLE DELETE` grant, so the old call answers 403.

### Additive

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `LabelService` | `getLabel` only, raw-key fallback | + `requireLabel(domain, key)` (throws when the domain is not loaded or lacks the key), + `options(domain)` → `LabelOption[]` `{code, caption}` sorted by caption |
| table-action parameters | no file input | `dataType: 'file'` renders a file picker; a body with a file posts as `multipart/form-data` |
| partner documents | none | `PartnerDocumentService` (`list`, `pending`, `upload`, `previewUrl`, `review`), `<sail-document-upload>`, `<sail-partner-documents>` and `<sail-document-review-queue>` over keel's generic REST table and `DocumentHandler` |

### Behavioral

- `RealtimeService.userFrames()` now passes user frames that carry an `op` (keel's `{op: "notification"}`); only `subscribed` / `unsubscribed` / `error` are treated as control frames.
- After the first successful `load()`, `NotificationInboxService` re-fetches the newest page on each realtime `notification` frame and merges it over the cache head. The app still calls `RealtimeService.connect()`; `reset()` drops the subscription.

## Adopting it

1. Rename `delete(id)` → `remove(id)` and `(deleted)` → `(removed)`. Mount keel's `UserPaymentMethodHandler` routes (v1.2.79).
2. For generic-table uploads, seed a table-level `upload` action and parameters including `file`, then mount `DocumentHandler.Upload` at that path behind `WrapTableAction`.

migrations.title: Table actions collect parameters; a stat tile
migrations.summary: An action that declares parameters (keel v1.2.75) opens a dialog and posts the values merged with the record key. <sail-stat-tile> renders one preformatted number with target, progress, delta and a trend sparkline.
migrations.body_markdown:
### Additive

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `TableAction` | no inputs beside the key | + `parameters?: TableActionParameter[]` (`name`, `caption`, `dataType`, `required`, `lookupTable?`) |
| dashboard number | app-local markup | `<sail-stat-tile label value [target] [progress] [delta] [deltaGood] [trend]>` |

### Behavioral

`BaseTable.executeAction` opens a parameter dialog for an action with `parameters`, shows `confirmMessage` inside it instead of `confirm()`, and posts `{...primaryKeyValues(record), ...values}`. Actions without parameters are unchanged. Requires keel v1.2.75 for the metadata; older servers send none and nothing changes.

migrations.title: Off-session SCA refusals are a first-class charge outcome
migrations.summary: ChargeStatus gains 'authentication_required' and ChargeResult gains paymentMethodId, so an off-session charge the issuer refused for SCA no longer decodes as a plain failure. ScaConfirmer requires confirmWithMethod for on-session re-confirmation; <sail-sca-confirm> picks the operation from the status. Requires keel v1.2.70+ to produce the status. sourceState() maps analytic source headers and rows to card state, message, and CTA.
migrations.body_markdown:
### Breaking

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `ScaConfirmer` had one method, `confirm(clientSecret)` | a second, `confirmWithMethod(clientSecret, paymentMethodId)`, is required |

Every `ScaConfirmer` implementation must add it. There is no default and no
optional shim: an implementation that cannot re-confirm would send an
`authentication_required` charge down the failure branch, which is the bug this
release fixes.

```ts
async confirmWithMethod(clientSecret: string, paymentMethodId: string): Promise<ScaResult> {
  const stripe = await this.getStripe();
  if (!stripe) return { outcome: 'failed', error: 'Payment library failed to load.' };
  const { error } = await stripe.confirmCardPayment(clientSecret, { payment_method: paymentMethodId });
  return error ? { outcome: 'failed', error: error.message } : { outcome: 'succeeded' };
}
```

### Additive

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `ChargeStatus` | `'succeeded' \| 'requires_action' \| 'failed'` | + `'authentication_required'` |
| `ChargeResult` | no refused-method field | + `paymentMethodId?: string` |
| `<sail-sca-confirm>` | one action state | dispatches on status; a confirm button renders for both action states |
| analytic source → card state | app-local mapping | + `sourceState(result, sourceName, connectLabel?)` → `SourceCardState` `{ state, message, cta }`: `NOT_CONNECTED` offers the CTA, `NOT_COLLECTED` leaves it empty, anything else is `ready` / `empty` from the rows |

## Adopting it

1. Return the new status from your charge endpoint. keel `payment.ChargeClient`
   already produces it (keel **v1.2.70+**) — pass `Status` and `PaymentMethodID`
   through as camelCase `status` / `paymentMethodId`.

```jsonc
{ "status": "authentication_required", "clientSecret": "pi_..._secret_...", "paymentMethodId": "pm_..." }
```

2. Delete any app-local widening of `ChargeStatus` / `ChargeResult` and bind
   `<sail-sca-confirm>` to the result as before — the component picks the
   operation from the status, so the template does not change.

### Notes

- An off-session refusal carries no `next_action`, so the component never takes
  the `actionUrl` redirect branch for it, even if the field is populated.
- `authentication_required` needs both `clientSecret` and `paymentMethodId`. A
  result missing either fails loudly through `(failed)` instead of confirming
  the wrong thing.

migrations.title: Notification inbox client and an optional no-source CTA
migrations.summary: NotificationInboxService and NotificationCenterComponent speak keel v1.2.71's InboxHandler contract - a typed page, per-message and whole-inbox mark-read, and a shared unread count a toolbar badge can bind to. The no-source CTA on DataCardComponent and NoSourceOverlayComponent becomes optional: an empty label renders the state without a button, for a source whose collector does not exist yet. Both are additive; existing call sites keep their behavior.
migrations.body_markdown:
## What changed

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| notification inbox | none | + `NotificationInboxService` and `NotificationCenterComponent` (`sail-notification-center`) over keel's `InboxHandler`; + `InboxMessage` / `InboxPage`; + `notificationsURL`, `notificationsMarkReadURL`, `notificationsMarkAllReadURL` on `RestURL` |
| `DataCardComponent` `no-source` | the connect button always rendered | `[connectLabel]=""` renders the state with no button |
| `NoSourceOverlayComponent` | the CTA always rendered | `[ctaLabel]=""` renders the overlay with no button |

## Adopting the notification inbox

1. Mount keel's `InboxHandler` (keel **v1.2.71** or later). The defaults match its
   routes; an app that mounts it elsewhere overrides the three paths:

```ts
configureRestUrls(host, { notificationsURL: '/api/v2/notifications', notificationsMarkReadURL: '/api/v2/notifications/mark_read', notificationsMarkAllReadURL: '/api/v2/notifications/mark_all_read' });
```

2. Delete the app-local notification client and render the center:

```html
<sail-notification-center heading="Notifications" (selected)="open($event)" />
```

What a message means stays downstream: `(selected)` hands you the `InboxMessage`
and you route on its `type` / `data`.

3. A toolbar badge reads the same cache the center fills, rather than fetching
   again:

```ts
readonly unread = inject(NotificationInboxService).unreadCount;   // Signal<number>
```

4. Call `reset()` on logout. The cache is per-session, and nothing clears it for you.

### Notes

- Message ids are `BIGINT` server-side and travel as **strings**. Keep them strings —
  a JS number cannot hold one — and pass `message.id` straight back to `markRead`.
- keel answers both mark-read routes with `204`, so the cache is updated locally
  instead of re-fetched. A message the cache has never seen leaves `unreadCount`
  untouched.
- `load()` / `loadMore()` default to 20 messages; keel caps a page at 100 and the
  client clamps to match, so `hasMore` reflects what the server actually applied.
- Nothing pushes an inbox message. Call `load()` again to pick up new ones.

## Adopting the optional no-source CTA

The `no-source` state covers both a provider that is not connected and one whose
collector does not exist yet. Only the first has anything to connect, and a button
that fixes nothing costs a support ticket. Pass an empty label for the second:

```html
<sail-data-card [state]="state()" [connectLabel]="hasCollector() ? 'Connect' : ''" ... />
```

Existing call sites keep their button — the defaults are unchanged.

migrations.title: Domain-verification component and a conversation transport for Scout's HTTP bridge
migrations.summary: DomainVerificationComponent renders the send-code -> confirm flow over the new DOMAIN_VERIFIER port, and VerificationFlowComponent gains an optional resend cooldown and code expiry. ConversationService in @nauticana/sail/agent speaks Scout's fixed conversation contract - submit, an SSE stream that feeds a TurnStream, and cancel - so the transport is no longer app-owned. Both are additive: existing call sites keep their behavior.
migrations.body_markdown:
## What changed

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| domain ownership | none | + `DomainVerificationComponent` (`sail-domain-verification`) and the `DOMAIN_VERIFIER` port (`requestVerification(domain)`, `confirm(domain, code)`) |
| `VerificationFlowComponent` | resend always enabled, no expiry, `errorMessage` rendered only in the code step | + `[resendAfterSeconds]`, `[codeExpiresInSeconds]` (both default `0` = today's behavior); `errorMessage` now also renders in the `idle` step |
| conversation transport | app-owned | + `ConversationService` in `@nauticana/sail/agent`: `submit`, `stream(requestId, turnStream)`, `cancel`, mounted at `CONVERSATION_BASE_PATH` |
| SSE | none | + `SseParser`, and the wire types `ConversationTurnRequest`, `ConversationTurnAccepted`, `ConversationStreamError`, `ConversationStreamFailure` |

## Adopting the domain-verification component

1. Provide the port from whatever service already calls your endpoints — any object with the two methods satisfies it:

```ts
providers: [{ provide: DOMAIN_VERIFIER, useExisting: RegistrationService }]
```

`requestVerification` and `confirm` may emit any body; the component reads only success or failure and reports the failure through `errorDetail()`.

2. Replace the hand-rolled domain field, verify button, code field and confirm button with one element:

```html
<sail-domain-verification
  [domain]="domainUrl()"
  [resendAfterSeconds]="60"
  (domainChange)="form.controls.domainUrl.setValue($event)"
  (verified)="domainVerified.set(true)" />
```

Editing the domain returns the flow to `idle`, because a code is bound to the domain it was issued for. Style `.domain-verification*` and the `.verification-*` hooks it composes.

## Adopting the conversation transport

1. Provide the mount point. The default is Scout's `/api/conversation/`; a product surface is a value provider:

```ts
providers: [{ provide: CONVERSATION_BASE_PATH, useValue: '/api/wingmate/' }]
```

2. Delete the app-local fetch/SSE/cursor code and submit through the service, then stream into a `TurnStream`:

```ts
const stream = new TurnStream(requestId);
this.conversation.submit({ request_id: requestId, conversation_id: conversationId, agent_id: 'wingmate', input })
  .pipe(switchMap(() => this.conversation.stream(requestId, stream)), takeUntilDestroyed())
  .subscribe({ error: (err) => this.onStreamError(err) });
```

3. Handle the two failures that are not transport noise. A `ConversationStreamFailure` with status `410` means the replay window expired while the turn is still running, so no stored result exists yet — the service has already called `markReplayExpired()`; stream again later and the backend answers the same cursor with the stored final frame. Any other status is the `event: error` frame's status.

4. Reconnect by calling `stream(requestId, stream)` again. The cursor is `stream.cursor()` unchanged; a suspension frame does not advance it, so a reconnect after an approval is decided picks up the resumed frame at the same sequence.

5. `cancel(requestId)` only requests the stop — call `stream.markCancelRequested()` and wait for the final frame, as `sail-turn-stream-view` already documents.

## Notes

- The stream cannot use `EventSource`, which sends no `Authorization` header, so it is a `fetch` body reader that carries the bearer itself and rotates it once through `BaseAuthService.refreshSession()` on a `401`. The auth interceptor's circuit breaker does not cover it.
- `submit` and `cancel` are ordinary `HttpClient` calls, so interceptors and the `{data, meta}` envelope unwrapping apply as usual.
- Backend alignment: Scout `v0.7.1` or later (`POST {base}turn`, `GET {base}turn/stream?request_id=&cursor=`, `POST {base}turn/cancel`).

migrations.title: TurnStream uses Scout's zero-based next-sequence cursor and keeps a suspended turn open
migrations.summary: TurnStream now accepts Scout reply sequence 0 and exposes cursor() as the next sequence wanted, matching Scout ConversationHandler's inclusive replay cursor. A suspension frame no longer ends the stream or advances the cursor.
migrations.body_markdown:
## Breaking

| Old | New |
|---|---|
| `TurnStream.cursor()` was the last rendered sequence, starting at 0 | the next sequence wanted, starting at 0 (`lastSequence + 1`) |

`TurnStream` previously initialized its last rendered sequence to 0, which dropped Scout's first frame, and exposed the last rendered sequence as its replay cursor, which replayed that frame.

## Behavioral

A frame whose last event is `approval_pending` is a suspension: Scout marks it `final` with an `error_code` and the resumed turn reuses its sequence. `TurnStream` now reports `awaiting_approval` for it instead of `failed`, does not advance `cursor()`, drops a replay of the same suspension, accepts the resumed frame at that sequence, and leaves it out of `finalFrame`.

## Migration

1. Pass `stream.cursor()` directly as the `cursor` query parameter of Scout's conversation stream endpoint. Remove any caller-side increment.
2. After a suspension frame the server closes the delivery; reconnect from `stream.cursor()` once the approval is decided.

migrations.title: Secondary entry point @nauticana/sail/agent; package exports close deep imports
migrations.summary: Agent Studio (studio-v2) models, AgentStudioService, the prompt layer editor, release provenance, typed turn events, TurnStream resume/cancel state, and a decision timeline ship under a new entry point, @nauticana/sail/agent, which the root barrel does not export — apps that do not import it bundle none of it. package.json now declares `exports` (only `.` and `./agent`) and `sideEffects`.
migrations.body_markdown:
## What changed

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| entry points | any path under the package resolved | `exports`: `@nauticana/sail` and `@nauticana/sail/agent` only |
| deep imports | `@nauticana/sail/service/<file>`, `@nauticana/sail/model/<file>`, `@nauticana/sail/component/...` | import the same symbol from `@nauticana/sail` — every public symbol is in the root barrel |
| `sideEffects` | unset (every module kept) | `["./src/model/decorator.ts"]`; bundlers may drop unused root-barrel modules |
| agent UI | none | `@nauticana/sail/agent` (see README, *Agent UI*) |

## Steps

1. Search for `from '@nauticana/sail/` and rewrite every match other than `@nauticana/sail/agent` to `from '@nauticana/sail'`. A wildcard tsconfig `paths` entry (`@nauticana/sail/*`) bypasses `exports`, so the compiler will not flag these — search explicitly, then remove the wildcard mapping.
2. To use the agent UI, add the tsconfig path `"@nauticana/sail/agent": ["./node_modules/@nauticana/sail/src/agent/index"]` and import from `@nauticana/sail/agent`.
3. Apps that do not use the agent UI need no further change. `src/agent/` is still type-checked where the app's tsconfig includes `sail/src/**/*.ts`; it is never bundled.

migrations.title: Source-readiness card state, analytic source status, grouped bulk action, before/after diff
migrations.summary: DataCardState gains 'no-source' with a matching NoSourceOverlayComponent, so an included-but-unconnected feature shows a connect prompt instead of an upgrade prompt. BaseRestService.analyticWithStatus() returns the rows together with the X-Data-Source-Status / X-Data-Source response headers; analytic() is unchanged. GroupedBulkActionComponent runs one action per group of rows and reports partial success; BeforeAfterDiffComponent / wordDiff() render a word-level diff.
migrations.body_markdown:
## What changed

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `DataCardState` | `loading \| ready \| empty \| error \| locked` | + `no-source` |
| `DataCardComponent` | — | + `[sourceName]`, `[noSourceMessage]`, `[connectLabel]` inputs and a `connect` output, rendered in the `no-source` state (`.data-card-no-source`); the chart template is not instantiated |
| source-readiness gate | only `LockedOverlayComponent` (upgrade prompt) | + `NoSourceOverlayComponent` (`sail-no-source-overlay`): `[unavailable]`, `[sourceName]`, `[message]`, `[ctaLabel]`, `connect`; the protected `<ng-template>` is never instantiated while unavailable |
| `BaseRestService` | `analytic<T>(): Observable<T[]>` discards the response | + protected `analyticWithStatus<T>(): Observable<AnalyticResult<T>>` = `{ rows, source: { status, id } }` from `X-Data-Source-Status` / `X-Data-Source`; `analytic<T>()` still returns `T[]`. New exported types `AnalyticResult`, `AnalyticSourceStatus` |
| bulk table action | none | + `GroupedBulkActionComponent` (`sail-grouped-bulk-action`) with `BulkActionGroup`, `BulkActionResult`, `BulkActionCompletion`, `BulkGroupKey`; all copy is supplied through inputs |
| diff rendering | none | + `BeforeAfterDiffComponent` (`sail-before-after-diff`) and the pure `wordDiff()` helper with `DiffToken` / `DiffTokenKind` |

## Migration steps for downstream consumers

1. Code that is exhaustive over `DataCardState` (a `switch` with a `never` check, a `Record<DataCardState, …>`) must add a `'no-source'` branch.
2. To use source status, have the backend set `X-Data-Source-Status` (and optionally `X-Data-Source`) on analytic responses. When the app and API are on different origins the backend must also send `Access-Control-Expose-Headers: X-Data-Source-Status, X-Data-Source`; otherwise the browser hides both headers and `source.status` is `null`.
3. Map the status to `state="no-source"` and handle `(connect)`; do not reuse `locked` / `(upgrade)` for a missing source.
4. Replace app-local batch-approval UI with `<sail-grouped-bulk-action>`: `[execute]` returns `Observable<{ attempted, succeeded }>`; refresh `[rows]` on `(finished)`. The outcome message renders above the groups and persists until the next action, so it remains visible after the refresh removes the group.
5. Replace app-local diff code with `<sail-before-after-diff>` or `wordDiff()`, and style `ins.diff-add` / `del.diff-del` / `.diff-same` in the app stylesheet.

## Breaking-change risk

Limited source-level break: exhaustive `DataCardState` switches and `Record<DataCardState, …>` declarations must add the `no-source` state (step 1). Existing non-exhaustive consumers continue to compile, and the remaining APIs are additive.

migrations.title: Refresh-token rotation, server-side logout, setup intents, realtime client (keel v1.2.58)
migrations.summary: Adopts keel v1.2.57/v1.2.58. Every login path stores the refreshToken keel now returns; authInterceptor rotates it at /public/token/refresh on a 401 and replays the request, so short JWT lifetimes no longer log users out. logout() revokes the refresh token at /public/logout. BillingService.createSetupIntent() wraps /api/billing/setup-intent. RealtimeService is the client for keel's realtime.Hub at /public/ws.
migrations.body_markdown:
## What changed

| | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Login responses (`login`, `loginWithGoogle`, `verify2FALogin`, `verifyBackupCode`, `verifyOtp`, `loginSocial`) | only `token` was stored | `refreshToken` (keel v1.2.57+) is stored beside it; `LoginResponse2FA`, `TwoFactorVerifyResponse`, `OtpVerifyResponse`, `LoginResponseSocial` gain `refreshToken?`; new `TokenPair` model |
| `authInterceptor` on 401 | counted toward the 5-in-10s circuit; the user was logged out once the JWT expired | first calls `BaseAuthService.refreshSession()` (one shared `POST /public/token/refresh`), stores the rotated pair, replays the request with the new JWT. A 401 from the refresh itself ends the session (`sessionExpired()`); other refresh failures keep the session and count the original 401 as before |
| `BaseAuthService` | — | + `refreshSession(): Observable<string>`; `acceptToken(token, refreshToken?)` — omitting the refresh token drops any stored one, so a handoff never keeps another account's refresh token; `logout()` posts `{refreshToken}` to `/public/logout` (best effort) before `clearSession()`, which now also drops `localStorage.refreshToken` |
| `RestURL` | — | + `tokenRefreshURL` (`/public/token/refresh`), `logoutURL` (`/public/logout`), `realtimeURL` (`/public/ws`), `setupIntentURL` (`/api/billing/setup-intent`) |
| `BillingService` | no setup-intent client; apps hand-rolled the call behind `UserPaymentMethodsComponent`'s add button | + `createSetupIntent(): Observable<SetupIntentResponse>` (`{setupIntentId, clientSecret, customerId, ephemeralKey}`); the provider payment sheet stays app-owned |
| realtime | each app wrote its own WebSocket client | + `RealtimeService` (root): `connect()` / `disconnect()`, `channel<T>(name)`, `userFrames<T>()`, `unsubscribe(name)`, `send(frame)`, `connected` and `lastError` signals; JWT via `?token=`, reconnect with backoff, re-subscribe after reconnect |

## Migration steps for downstream consumers

1. Upgrade the backend to keel v1.2.58 and mount `PublicHandler.GetPublicRoutes()` (or at least `/public/token/refresh` and `/public/logout`). Against an older keel, `refreshToken` is absent, no refresh is attempted, and behaviour is identical to 1.1.17.
2. Delete any app-local refresh-token or 401-retry interceptor; `authInterceptor` now owns both. Keep it registered before app interceptors that read the `Authorization` header.
3. Handoff flows that call `acceptToken(token)` should pass the refresh token as the second argument when the minting endpoint returns one (keel `AbstractHandler.SessionTokens`).
4. Replace app-local calls to `/api/billing/setup-intent` with `BillingService.createSetupIntent()`; keep the provider SDK call that opens the sheet in the app.
5. To use the realtime hub, mount keel's `handler.WebSocketHandler` at `/public/ws`, call `realtime.connect()` after login and `disconnect()` in `logout()` overrides, and consume `realtime.channel<T>('order:42')`. Override `RestURL.realtimeURL` via `configureRestUrls` if the hub is mounted elsewhere.
6. Sessions now survive JWT expiry; if the app relied on `session_timeout` as an idle logout, enforce idle timeout in the app or shorten `refresh_token_ttl` on the keel side.

## Breaking-change risk

None to compile. Behavioral: a stale JWT is refreshed instead of logging the user out, and `logout()` issues one extra request. `login?sessionExpired=true` now means the refresh token itself was rejected.

migrations.title: errorDetail distinguishes transport and non-API failures from backend rejections; isTransportFailure
migrations.summary: errorDetail no longer returns the caller's fallback for a network failure, a CORS-blocked response or a proxy error page; the new isTransportFailure(err) predicate exposes the status-0 case. v1.1.16 is the same content republished with a corrected package version.
migrations.body_markdown:
## What changed

| Area | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `util/errors` — error-detail-transport (behavioral) | errorDetail(err, fallback) returned the caller's fallback whenever the error carried no RFC 7807 detail. A network failure, a CORS-blocked response and a proxy error page were therefore indistinguishable from a backend rejection, and the fallback string ("Could not save", "Registration failed") misattributed the fault to the API. | errorDetail reports the two non-API cases distinctly: a transport failure (Angular status 0 — network down, CORS blocked, request aborted) returns "Cannot reach the server — the network or a CORS rule blocked the response.", and an unreadable body carrying a real status returns "<fallback> (HTTP <status>)". Bodies that do carry detail/title/message are unaffected. The new isTransportFailure(err) predicate exposes the status-0 case so callers can branch on it instead of matching the message text. |

## Migration steps for downstream consumers

1. Delete app-local wrappers around errorDetail that added this discrimination and call errorDetail directly.
2. Update tests that assert the exact fallback string for a status-0 or non-JSON-body case.

## Breaking-change risk

None to compile; messages only change for the two non-API cases.

migrations.title: Agency self-service UI over keel v1.2.41
migrations.summary: AgencyService and seven composable agency components (status banner, clients, accept-invitation, earnings summary, commission ledger, payout history, payout profile) replace app-copied agency screens. Statuses come from keel basis constant domains; the commercial model is the simplified frozen-rate contract; money is per-currency minor units.
migrations.body_markdown:
Requires keel v1.2.41 (the invitation-accept flow branches on RFC 7807 code `agency_no_partner`) and the basis seed shipped since keel v1.2.40.

## What changed

| Area | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `agency` — agency-ui (additive) | Each app maintained its own agency REST client, invitation page, client book, commission tables, payout history, and status labels. | AgencyService and seven composable agency components are exported. Statuses come from keel constant catalogues, extra client columns are injected, and routes/brand/global CSS stay app-owned. |
| `agency/service` — agency-enroll-method (breaking) | Downstream copies could call AgencyService.enrollReferral(). | The shared service exposes the commercial-model-neutral AgencyService.enroll() method only. |
| `agency/status` — agency-status-domains (breaking) | Downstream agency screens could use app-local status domain ids such as billing_model or commission_status. | StatusChipComponent uses keel basis domains agency_client_status, agency_billing_model, agency_commission_status, and agency_payout_status. |
| `agency/models` — agency-simplified-rate-model (breaking) | Downstream UIs could expose partner_client, partner_delegation, agency_commission_customer, agency_wholesale_enrollment, or commission-rule/tier/fixed-rate concepts. | The contract uses agency_client_invitation, agency_client_delegation, agency_client_rate, and agency_profile.wholesaleAllowed. Rates are frozen percentage basis points; there is no rule-schedule DTO or UI. |
| `agency/payout` — agency-money-and-payout-profile (behavioral) | Agency totals were commonly divided by 100 and summed without regard to currency; payout destinations were admin-only CRUD. | AgencyEarnings contains one balance per currency, formatMinorCurrency is exponent-aware, and AgencyPayoutProfileComponent selects only the authenticated user's fully onboarded destination while composing provider onboarding. |

## Migration steps for downstream consumers

1. Upgrade the backend to keel v1.2.41 (the invitation-accept flow branches on its RFC 7807 code 'agency_no_partner'), replace copied UI incrementally, and mount app-owned /agency and /agency/accept routes. Override RestURL.agency*URL if the backend is not mounted at /api/v1. Load keel basis_seed.yml (shipped since v1.2.40) so the canonical agency status domains are present.
2. Rename enrollReferral() calls to enroll(); no compatibility alias is shipped.
3. Load keel v1.2.40 basis_seed.yml and remove divergent app-local ids. Values are client S/I/V/X; billing R/W; commission H/P/R/D/O; payout C/P/D/F/R/V/M.
4. Rename imports and app-specific labels, remove rule/tier/fixed-rate screens, and treat wholesaleAllowed as permission for a per-client switch—not as the agency's global billing model.
5. Do not sum balances across currencies. Wire sealed tax-id storage in keel before enabling bank replacement, and style the new agency-* / commission-ledger classes in the app's global stylesheet.

Compile break for apps that called `enrollReferral()` or imported the pre-1.1.14 agency DTO names; no compatibility aliases ship. Apps with app-local agency status domain ids must switch to the keel basis domains.
